audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Akali levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items, while the prose (whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], early, mid, late) says Maokai owns 2-5 and still wins the straight 1v1 at two items. The packet levelChart and the 54.09% win rate over 159 games back the prose, not the chart.
audit.why: The page told a Maokai player he loses the exact levels the same page tells him to trade in.
audit.corrected: Rows 1,2,3,5,6 flipped in both layers to Maokai/Maokai/Maokai/Skill/Maokai; row 4 flipped to Akali (her R spike, which whys[4] and spikes[1] already describe). Row 0 left as Skill — both layers agree and the prose calls it even.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why gave no reason for the level-6 swing and did not name Perfect Execution.
audit.why: Her 6 is the one row she takes: two dashes plus an execute against a 130s Nature's Grasp.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Perfect Execution and the 130s R cost of spending it early.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Untargetable inside. W-root needs a target' was stated but never given a cooldown, and Twisted Advance's own untargetable dash was absent.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20s at rank 1 falling to 16s, Shuriken Flip 16s — those two are the whole reason a trade window exists. Twisted Advance is untargetable through the dash, so it rides out her burst; shroud is the only thing that breaks its target-lock.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[1].why, phases[3].why and report[5].t now carry the numbers and the untargetable-dash interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown figures anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Maokai's W drops to 11s at rank 4 while shroud is still 17s — a free trade every rotation, which is why 4-5 is his.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Akali's Twilight Shroud is down.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is point-and-click — shroud is her only escape, and at rank 1 that is a 20s hole. Trade the moment it is down.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twilight Shroud's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your root falls to 11s at rank 4 while shroud is still 17s — that gap is a free trade every rotation. Freeze and repeat it, don't chase.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Akali's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Perfect Execution gives her two dashes and an execute — her first real all-in. Nature's Grasp is 130s, so spend it on the kill, not chip.

edits.before: - Akali Twilight Shroud: matchup-defining — Untargetable inside. W-root needs a target. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Twilight Shroud: 20s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — untargetable inside it, and Twisted Advance needs a target. - Shuriken Flip: 16s, her only other escape. - Nature's Grasp: 130s — kill windows only, never chip.

edits.before: Untargetable inside. W-root needs a target. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Untargetable inside it, and your W needs a target. It is 20s at rank 1 — bait it.

edits.before: Track Akali's Twilight Shroud: Untargetable inside. W-root needs a target. When it is down — W-Q + R her.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable mid-dash, so it rides out her R burst; shroud alone breaks its target-lock.

notes: Per the mirror audit, Maokai's Bramble Smash carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's description (knockback, damage, slow) does not support, so nothing here claims Q can deny Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution. Chart rows were proposed as one paired group across both layers. Row 0 left untouched: packet says Maokai but both layers and the prose say even, and I would not flip it on the packet alone.
